h1:
Koh Larn Seafood
The Restaurants People Actually Go To
intro: Koh Larn sits right off Pattaya, and the ferry from Bali Hai Pier gets you there in under an hour. Once you step off the boat, the first thing a lot of people want is a seafood lunch by the water. We pulled together the seafood spots people actually go to and review again and again, mostly around Tawaen Beach and Na Baan, with the area each one sits in, the dishes people order most, and rough prices so you can size up your budget before you sit down.
chips: 💸 From a hundred baht a plate to four figures

blocks.html: Koh Larn seafood isn't about some complicated secret recipe. The selling point is freshness, sea breeze, and a beach view. Prices on the island run a touch higher than the Pattaya side because everything has to be ferried over, but if you pick the right place and order smart, you can eat well on a budget you can live with. We ranked these from real reviews on Wongnai, Trip.com, and Pantip threads, weighting freshness, cooking, location, and value for money.

blocks.title: How to read the prices in this article
blocks.html: The prices here are rough ranges from recent reviews. Seafood is seasonal and sold by actual weight, so prices move all the time. Most places charge prawns, shellfish, and crab by the kilo or half-kilo, so ask the price per kilo and have it weighed in front of you before you order — that way there are no surprises when the bill comes.

items.name: Krua Chaliang Lom
items.blurb: The most talked-about spot on the island, right on the water in the Wiang Ao area, with a breezy waterfront "Chaliang Lom" corner. The dishes people order most are prawns fried in tamarind sauce, soft-shell crab with curry powder, old-school fried sea bass, and lotus-stem som tam with fresh prawns — bold flavors, proper Thai cooking. No reservations, walk-in only, so on weekends it fills up fast; go before noon.
items.meta: Wiang Ao area · open 09:30–22:00 · no reservations
items.price: From ฿80 a plate · whole table ฿400–900/person

items.name: Suk Samoe Camping
items.blurb: A camping-style spot on Tawaen Beach with plenty of tables right on the sand, plus live music and a cocktail bar in the evening — good for settling in and waiting for sunset. The seafood is very fresh, and reviews single out the squid sashimi, mantis-shrimp sashimi, clear seafood tom yum, crab fried rice, and sea bass with fish sauce. Great atmosphere, though pricier than the island average.
items.meta: Tawaen Beach · open into the evening · live music
items.price: Tom yum ฿300 · crab fried rice ฿200 · sea bass ฿600

items.name: Krua Rabiang Rak
items.blurb: A waterfront seafood spot in the Na Baan area — chill, breezy, with a lovely sunset view. It's strongest on prawns and crab, cooked fresh to order. Reviewers love the 5–6pm window when the light softens and the view is at its best. Good for couples or small groups.
items.meta: Na Baan area · best view in the evening

items.name: Fresh seafood market by Wat Mai Samran (weigh-and-cook stalls)
items.blurb: Not a fancy sit-down place, but the spot budget eaters love. The market is by Wat Mai Samran, near the Na Baan pier, with stalls displaying tanks of squid and fish so you pick your own catch, then they weigh it and cook it to order — fried, grilled, steamed, or boiled, paid by actual weight. Busiest Friday through Sunday and public holidays. Great if you want to see the seafood before you pay.
items.meta: By Wat Mai Samran, near Na Baan pier · busy Fri–Sun
items.price: Seafood ฿200–1,000 by weight · spicy soup ฿100

items.name: Saudi Seafood
items.blurb: A waterfront seafood restaurant about 1km from Tawaen Beach. What reviewers like is the good location at friendlier prices than a lot of places on the island. General fresh seafood menu — prawns, shellfish, fish, squid. Good if you want to eat by the water without paying too much.

items.name: Krua Chalita
items.blurb: A spot near the pier. Reviewers mention the prawns with curry powder and the blue-crab som tam — solid cooking, prices that won't sting. Handy for a meal before or after the ferry, no long walk from the pier.
items.meta: Near the pier · easy stop before or after the ferry

items.name: Nong Riew
items.blurb: A spot on the road to Nuan Beach, focused on simple fresh seafood. Reviewers order the fresh prawn yum, steamed shellfish, and seafood tom yum — mild, easy-eating flavors. Good for a stop on the way to the quieter Nuan Beach side.
items.meta: On the road to Nuan Beach · simple fresh cooking

items.name: Je Paet Seafood
items.blurb: An old-school seafood spot that islanders and regular visitors know. Focused on fresh prawns, shellfish, and squid, cooked fresh, home-style flavors at market prices. Good if you want straightforward seafood and don't care about a fancy setting.

items.name: To Kap Khao
items.blurb: A small place reviewers love for the juicy khanom jeen with crab curry sauce and one-plate seafood rice dishes. Good for a light meal or when you don't want to order a whole big table. Easy on the wallet.

items.name: Yok Yor Koh Larn
items.blurb: A cook-to-order spot near Tawaen Beach with good review scores. Good for groups who want to order a spread — prawns, shellfish, crab, and fish all on one table. Prices run mid to high depending on what you order.
items.meta: Near Tawaen Beach · order a spread

blocks.text: Pick a restaurant by area: Tawaen Beach vs Na Baan

blocks.html: Koh Larn has several beaches, but the seafood restaurants cluster in the two main areas people visit most. If you've already decided which beach you're hitting, pick a place in that area so you're not trekking across the island.

items: Tawaen Beach — the most popular beach, busy, with lots of beachfront spots like Suk Samoe Camping, Yok Yor, and others nearby. Best for settling in over seafood with a sea view.

Na Baan — the pier-and-village side, with both waterfront sit-down places like Krua Rabiang Rak and the fresh market by Wat Mai Samran where you can buy your catch and have it weighed and cooked. Good for budget eaters who want to see the seafood before they pay.
Wiang Ao area — Krua Chaliang Lom is around here, the famous spot people come specifically to eat at, on the water with a good breeze.
Toward Nuan Beach / Samae Beach — fewer places and quieter, good if you're dodging the crowds, but the choices are limited, so check the place is open before you head over.

blocks.text: The seafood dishes people order most on the island

blocks.html: If you're not sure what to order, these are the dishes that come up again and again in Koh Larn restaurant reviews. Order along these lines and you'll rarely go wrong.

items.name: Grilled prawns / prawns in tamarind sauce
items.blurb: Big fresh prawns, grilled or fried in sweet-sour tamarind sauce — the first dish almost every table orders. Priced by the kilo.

items.name: Steamed / grilled shellfish
items.blurb: Cockles, mussels, or whatever's in season, steamed with herbs or grilled over charcoal, dipped in seafood sauce — good value and easy to keep eating.

items.name: Steamed blue crab / soft-shell crab with curry powder
items.blurb: Steamed blue crab with dipping sauce, or soft-shell crab fried with curry powder and creamy egg — a dish Krua Chaliang Lom and several places do well.

items.name: Fried sea bass / with fish sauce
items.blurb: A whole sea bass, fried crisp with fish sauce or done old-school style, priced by the size of the fish — a centerpiece dish you can share.

items.name: Seafood tom yum / spicy soup
items.blurb: Clear or creamy tom yum loaded with prawns, squid, and shellfish — bold flavors that round out the meal. The spicy soup at the market starts at just a few hundred baht.

items.name: Squid / mantis-shrimp sashimi
items.blurb: Raw and fresh, for people who like sweet, tender seafood. Found at places confident in their freshness, like Suk Samoe — best eaten somewhere with fast turnover.

blocks.text: Eating Koh Larn seafood well and safely

blocks.title: Ask the price per kilo and have it weighed in front of you
blocks.html: Prawns, shellfish, and crab are mostly charged by weight. Before you order, ask the price per kilo and ask to have it weighed in front of you — that keeps your budget in check and means no confusion at the bill. Seasonal seafood prices move all the time.

blocks.title: Go early — fewer ferries and the restaurants are still fully stocked
blocks.html: Weekends get very busy, the ferries are packed, and the lines are long. Take one of the first ferries in the morning. Popular walk-in spots like Krua Chaliang Lom won't be slammed yet and will still have everything; by evening some places start running out of dishes.

items: Check freshness before you commit — look at the fish's eyes, the prawn shells, the smell of the shellfish. If it's not fresh, swap it out or skip the raw dishes.
Carry cash — some places and market stalls are mainly cash. Signal and card readers on the island aren't always reliable.
The sea can be murky some days, depending on the weather — if you're eating and swimming, check the forecast first; on windy, choppy days the view and the water won't be at their best.
Help keep the beach clean — pack out your trash or bin it properly when you're done, so Koh Larn's beaches stay clean.

blocks.html: Short version: if you want the famous, bold-flavored spot, go to Krua Chaliang Lom. If you want a long, beachfront vibe, go to Suk Samoe on Tawaen Beach. If you want to save money and pick your own catch, head to the fresh market by Wat Mai Samran in the Na Baan area. Choose by budget and style.

faq.q: Which Koh Larn seafood restaurant gets the most visitors?
faq.a: Krua Chaliang Lom in the Wiang Ao area is the most talked-about and most reviewed, known for its tamarind-sauce prawns and soft-shell crab with curry powder. It's walk-in only, no reservations, and it fills up on weekends, so go before noon. For a long beachfront vibe, people favor Suk Samoe Camping on Tawaen Beach.

faq.q: Is Koh Larn seafood expensive? How much should I budget?
faq.a: Prices on the island run a little higher than the Pattaya side because everything has to be ferried over. Single plates start around 80–250 THB, and if you sit down to a table of prawns, shellfish, crab, and fish, expect around 350–900 THB per person depending on what you order. To save money, go to the fresh market by Wat Mai Samran, pick your catch, and have it weighed and cooked by actual weight.

faq.q: Where can I buy fresh seafood to cook on Koh Larn?
faq.a: The fresh market by Wat Mai Samran, near the Na Baan pier, has stalls with tanks of squid and fish so you can pick your own catch, then have it weighed and cooked to order — fried, grilled, steamed, or boiled. Prices run from a few hundred up to around 1,000 THB by weight. The market is busiest Friday through Sunday and on public holidays.

faq.q: Tawaen Beach or Na Baan — where's better for seafood?
faq.a: Tawaen Beach is busy with lots of beachfront spots, strong on the long, sit-and-watch-the-sea atmosphere, like Suk Samoe and Yok Yor. Na Baan has both waterfront sit-down places like Krua Rabiang Rak and a fresh market where you buy your own catch at budget prices. Choose based on which beach you're heading to and your budget.

faq.q: Is it safe to eat sashimi or raw seafood on Koh Larn?
faq.a: It's fine at places with fast turnover that you trust on freshness, like spots reviewed for squid or mantis-shrimp sashimi such as Suk Samoe. Check how fresh the ingredients look before you order. If you're unsure or have a sensitive stomach, cooked dishes are the safer choice — and carry cash, since many places are mainly cash.
